Chunk.title: High Voltage (HV)
section_paths: High Voltage (HV) > Side Objectives > The End and pre-Moon Titanium
Chunk.text:
The End and pre-Moon Titanium
Diagram showing processing steps for making Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. EBF - Electric Blast Furnace; LCR - Large Chemical Reactor; DT - Distillation Tower.
Eyes of Ender can be made in an HV Chemical Reactor and used to find and activate the End Portal. After defeating the Ender Dragon, the player can travel to the Far End Asteroids where they will occasionally find veins of Naquadah Ore. This allows the player to produce Titanium Ingots without traveling to the Moon.
Raw Naquadah Ore goes through the usual ore processing and becomes Naquadah Oxide Mixture Dust. Two dust can be processed in the Electric Blast Furnace with 3000L of Fluoroantimonic Acid to produce 4 Titanium Trifluoride Dust, which is then put back into the EBF, which must be overclocked to EV , with 3000L of Hydrogen to get a Hot Titanium Ingot. Cool the ingot in a Vacuum Freezer to obtain a Titanium Ingot.
The production of Fluoroantimonic Acid is an involved process which requires a Large Chemical Reactor that is overclocked to EV. A Distillation Tower is not necessary for the production of Antimony Pentachloride but will refund all of the Ether used in the production of Antimony Trichloride Solution.
The diagram to the right shows the processing steps for obtaining Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. Note that Ethylene and Hydrogen Sulfide are considered inputs, rather than being part of the production chain, as they can be obtained in great quantities from processing Oil and its byproducts.

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2
Chunk.text:
Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.
For our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:
- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices, giving our 1-block controller control over a maximum of 192 devices.
- ME Drive. This will serve as an overflow buffer, just in case all your machines suffer maintenance issues and shutdown simultaneously.
- ME Storage Cell. Place inside the ME Drive. You will need at least 1.
- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.
- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).
- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.
Now, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:
- Galena Ore. oreGalena
- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena
- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena
- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena
- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena
- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena
- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena
- Galena Dust dustGalena
ME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Thus, when we place an OreDict card inside a ME Storage Bus facing towards an Input Bus, we have created an intelligent exporter of items!

Chunk.title: Low Voltage (LV)
section_paths: Low Voltage (LV) > Progression
Chunk.text:
Progression
Progression to MV requires the player to obtain 3 essential materials:
• Gallium -
There is no renewable way to obtain Gallium in LV. The best way is to electrolyze Sphalerite dust, giving an 11% chance for Gallium. Gallium is also obtainable as a byproduct of Zinc ore processing, Zinc Gravel can be purchased with Blacksmith coins at regular enough intervals that it shouldn't be a major issue for now. You can also use XP buckets if you're desperate. With an HV macerator you can obtain more byproducts from ore processing, making Gallium much easier to obtain.
• Arsenic -
Cobaltite is the primary way of obtaining Arsenic in LV. When Cobaltite is blasted in an EBF with oxygen it produces roasted cobalt and arsenic dust. Running roasted arsenic dust through the EBF again results in 3 arsenic ingots per 2 cobaltite. This process is oxygen neutral after electrolyzing the carbon dioxide produced.
• Aluminum -
Aluminum has 2 ways to be obtained in LV, one involves compressing Aluminum dust and blasting the "raw Aluminum" into 1 Aluminum ingot. This recipe is slow and not recommended. The other recipe uses 10 Alumina and 5 cryolite to produce 4 Aluminum ingots. While being more involved, this recipe offers much faster and more power efficient Aluminum.

Chunk.text:
MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line"
This shows the simplest version of a "central line" ore processing system. It has one route (priority -2) and is currently useless for anything practical. Gold chest = input and copper chest = output. This shows the second most basic EIO ore processing setup - a central line with an attached macerator round robin module.
EnderIO conduits are your first and cheapest option for creating a truly flexible ore processing system. This system is built around a " central conduit line " which all ores go through, and connected " modules " route ores into machines. Because of its modular nature, it is easy to add new routes or expand old ones. This is made possible due to the EIO conduit " priority " system, which allows us to make override routes.
The priority system for the " central line " design goes as follows:
Priority 0: Override routes. For example, specific ores, rare earths, etc.
Priority -1: Type filter routes. These are your "default" paths that are taken if nothing overrides them.
Priority -2: Output routes. This goes to the final output chest.
The simplest version of this is an input chest set to extract always, some conduits inbetween, and an output chest at -2 priority. Then everything you input (ores, random tinker tools by accident, w/e) will go to the output chest. But obviously this isn't very useful.
So you start adding " modules " to your inbetween conduits. These provide routes for ores to go. Let's start with a macerator module.

Chunk.title: High Voltage (HV)
section_paths: High Voltage (HV) > Side Objectives > The End and pre-Moon Titanium
Chunk.text:
The End and pre-Moon Titanium
Diagram showing processing steps for making Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. EBF - Electric Blast Furnace; LCR - Large Chemical Reactor; DT - Distillation Tower.
Eyes of Ender can be made in an HV Chemical Reactor and used to find and activate the End Portal. After defeating the Ender Dragon, the player can travel to the Far End Asteroids where they will occasionally find veins of Naquadah Ore. This allows the player to produce Titanium Ingots without traveling to the Moon.
Raw Naquadah Ore goes through the usual ore processing and becomes Naquadah Oxide Mixture Dust. Two dust can be processed in the Electric Blast Furnace with 3000L of Fluoroantimonic Acid to produce 4 Titanium Trifluoride Dust, which is then put back into the EBF, which must be overclocked to EV , with 3000L of Hydrogen to get a Hot Titanium Ingot. Cool the ingot in a Vacuum Freezer to obtain a Titanium Ingot.
The production of Fluoroantimonic Acid is an involved process which requires a Large Chemical Reactor that is overclocked to EV. A Distillation Tower is not necessary for the production of Antimony Pentachloride but will refund all of the Ether used in the production of Antimony Trichloride Solution.
The diagram to the right shows the processing steps for obtaining Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. Note that Ethylene and Hydrogen Sulfide are considered inputs, rather than being part of the production chain, as they can be obtained in great quantities from processing Oil and its byproducts.

Chunk.text:

For our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:
- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices, giving our 1-block controller control over a maximum of 192 devices.
- ME Drive. This will serve as an overflow buffer, just in case all your machines suffer maintenance issues and shutdown simultaneously.
- ME Storage Cell. Place inside the ME Drive. You will need at least 1.
- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.
- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).
- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.
Now, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:
- Galena Ore. oreGalena
- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena
- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena
- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena
- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena
- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena
- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena
- Galena Dust dustGalena
ME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Thus, when we place an OreDict card inside a ME Storage Bus facing towards an Input Bus, we have created an intelligent exporter of items!

Chunk.title: Insane Voltage (IV)
section_paths: Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines
Chunk.text:
Other chemical lines
Polybenzimidazole
Although the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.
Rare Earths
The rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank .

Chunk.text:
The End and pre-Moon Titanium
Diagram showing processing steps for making Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. EBF - Electric Blast Furnace; LCR - Large Chemical Reactor; DT - Distillation Tower.
Eyes of Ender can be made in an HV Chemical Reactor and used to find and activate the End Portal. After defeating the Ender Dragon, the player can travel to the Far End Asteroids where they will occasionally find veins of Naquadah Ore. This allows the player to produce Titanium Ingots without traveling to the Moon.
Raw Naquadah Ore goes through the usual ore processing and becomes Naquadah Oxide Mixture Dust. Two dust can be processed in the Electric Blast Furnace with 3000L of Fluoroantimonic Acid to produce 4 Titanium Trifluoride Dust, which is then put back into the EBF, which must be overclocked to EV , with 3000L of Hydrogen to get a Hot Titanium Ingot. Cool the ingot in a Vacuum Freezer to obtain a Titanium Ingot.
The production of Fluoroantimonic Acid is an involved process which requires a Large Chemical Reactor that is overclocked to EV. A Distillation Tower is not necessary for the production of Antimony Pentachloride but will refund all of the Ether used in the production of Antimony Trichloride Solution.
The diagram to the right shows the processing steps for obtaining Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. Note that Ethylene and Hydrogen Sulfide are considered inputs, rather than being part of the production chain, as they can be obtained in great quantities from processing Oil and its byproducts.

section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2
Chunk.text:
Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.
For our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:
- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices, giving our 1-block controller control over a maximum of 192 devices.
- ME Drive. This will serve as an overflow buffer, just in case all your machines suffer maintenance issues and shutdown simultaneously.
- ME Storage Cell. Place inside the ME Drive. You will need at least 1.
- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.
- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).
- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.
Now, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:
- Galena Ore. oreGalena
- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena
- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena
- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena
- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena
- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena
- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena
- Galena Dust dustGalena
ME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Thus, when we place an OreDict card inside a ME Storage Bus facing towards an Input Bus, we have created an intelligent exporter of items!

section_paths: Extreme Voltage (EV) > Progression > Side quest 2: Multiblock ore processing
Chunk.text:
Side quest 2: Multiblock ore processing
As you entered EV, you gained access to multiblock counterparts of centrifuge, thermal centrifuge, ore washer/chemical bath, and crusher. They are way more efficient compared to their singleblock variants, however they require large amounts of resources like Titanium and most are gated behind TPV coils, so they're listed here instead of in early EV. If your main resource income is from bees, centrifuge is recommended over all other multiblocks as it speeds up centrifuging combs significantly.

Chunk.title: Insane Voltage (IV)
section_paths: Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines
Chunk.text:
Other chemical lines
Polybenzimidazole
Although the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.
Rare Earths
The rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank .

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Flexible
Chunk.text:
Flexible
Ores in GT: New Horizons have multiple " routes " you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the "best" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):
- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)
- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)
- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)
While for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.
Every ore in the game will have a different "optimal" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.
You also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators.

Chunk.text:
MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line"
This shows the simplest version of a "central line" ore processing system. It has one route (priority -2) and is currently useless for anything practical. Gold chest = input and copper chest = output. This shows the second most basic EIO ore processing setup - a central line with an attached macerator round robin module.
EnderIO conduits are your first and cheapest option for creating a truly flexible ore processing system. This system is built around a " central conduit line " which all ores go through, and connected " modules " route ores into machines. Because of its modular nature, it is easy to add new routes or expand old ones. This is made possible due to the EIO conduit " priority " system, which allows us to make override routes.
The priority system for the " central line " design goes as follows:
Priority 0: Override routes. For example, specific ores, rare earths, etc.
Priority -1: Type filter routes. These are your "default" paths that are taken if nothing overrides them.
Priority -2: Output routes. This goes to the final output chest.
The simplest version of this is an input chest set to extract always, some conduits inbetween, and an output chest at -2 priority. Then everything you input (ores, random tinker tools by accident, w/e) will go to the output chest. But obviously this isn't very useful.
So you start adding " modules " to your inbetween conduits. These provide routes for ores to go. Let's start with a macerator module.

Chunk.title: Insane Voltage (IV)
section_paths: Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines
Chunk.text:
Other chemical lines
Polybenzimidazole
Although the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.
Rare Earths
The rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank .

section_paths: Extreme Voltage (EV) > Progression > Side quest 2: Multiblock ore processing
Chunk.text:
Side quest 2: Multiblock ore processing
As you entered EV, you gained access to multiblock counterparts of centrifuge, thermal centrifuge, ore washer/chemical bath, and crusher. They are way more efficient compared to their singleblock variants, however they require large amounts of resources like Titanium and most are gated behind TPV coils, so they're listed here instead of in early EV. If your main resource income is from bees, centrifuge is recommended over all other multiblocks as it speeds up centrifuging combs significantly.

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Flexible
Chunk.text:
Flexible
Ores in GT: New Horizons have multiple " routes " you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the "best" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):
- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)
- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)
- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)
While for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.
Every ore in the game will have a different "optimal" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.
You also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators.

Chunk.text:
necessary in order to handle the large amounts of ores obtained by advanced Ore Drilling Plants and Void Miners.
An alternative to the ASIB in pre-LuV is the combination of the usage of the ME Export Bus with an ME OreDictionary Filter card set with the filter of "*", emulating the stocking of the ASIB by pushing the storage of the subnetwork to the input buses. However, a downside is that there is no benefit of immediate recipe checks unlike the ASIB, and the size of the input is limited to the slots of the input bus.
And like this, you now have an AE-linked ore processing machine capable of:
- Accepting both crushed ores (from ODPs) or whole ores (from VMs).
- Sifting appropriate ores capable of gem byproducts.
- Acquisition of tertiary byproducts from all possible ores (via thermal centrifuging and macerating of centrifuged ores)
- Export of dusts, gems (of all qualities), purified sphalerite and galena ores for indium processing, and crushed bastnasite and monazite for lanthanide processing.
Auxiliary ore processing setups that we can link to our main network, along with the useful OreDicts, are:
- Industrial Centrifuges to process Stone Dust ( dustStone ), Impure dusts ( dustImpure* ), Limonites ( dust*Limonite ), Metal Mixture Dust ( dustMetalMixture ), Sheldonite dusts ( dustCooperite ), and others
- Industrial Electrolyzers to process arbitrary dusts to recover purified elemental dusts and gases
- LCRs to process purified Sphalerite and purified Galena with sulfuric acid to get Indium Concentrate, and the subsequent precipitation using Aluminium dust to get Indium Dust and Lead-Zinc solution (can be electrolyzed to recover lead, silver, zinc, sulfur and water)
- OWP set to Chemical Bath mode with a screwdriver to process Rare Earth dusts with sulfuric acid and get Crushed Rare Earth ores. Feed these into the ore processing network to eventually recover Rare Earth (I) dusts which can be dehydrated to recover useful dusts (namely Yttrium).
- Platinum Processing Line , fed with the Platinum Metallic Powder Dust. Too long and complex to catalog here.
- Lanthanide Processing Line, fed with the crushed Bastnasite and crushed Monazite ores. Too long to catalog here.

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line"
Chunk.text:
MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line"
This shows the simplest version of a "central line" ore processing system. It has one route (priority -2) and is currently useless for anything practical. Gold chest = input and copper chest = output. This shows the second most basic EIO ore processing setup - a central line with an attached macerator round robin module.
EnderIO conduits are your first and cheapest option for creating a truly flexible ore processing system. This system is built around a " central conduit line " which all ores go through, and connected " modules " route ores into machines. Because of its modular nature, it is easy to add new routes or expand old ones. This is made possible due to the EIO conduit " priority " system, which allows us to make override routes.
The priority system for the " central line " design goes as follows:
Priority 0: Override routes. For example, specific ores, rare earths, etc.
Priority -1: Type filter routes. These are your "default" paths that are taken if nothing overrides them.
Priority -2: Output routes. This goes to the final output chest.
The simplest version of this is an input chest set to extract always, some conduits inbetween, and an output chest at -2 priority. Then everything you input (ores, random tinker tools by accident, w/e) will go to the output chest. But obviously this isn't very useful.
So you start adding " modules " to your inbetween conduits. These provide routes for ores to go. Let's start with a macerator module.

section_paths: High Voltage (HV) > Side Objectives > The End and pre-Moon Titanium
Chunk.text:
The End and pre-Moon Titanium
Diagram showing processing steps for making Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. EBF - Electric Blast Furnace; LCR - Large Chemical Reactor; DT - Distillation Tower.
Eyes of Ender can be made in an HV Chemical Reactor and used to find and activate the End Portal. After defeating the Ender Dragon, the player can travel to the Far End Asteroids where they will occasionally find veins of Naquadah Ore. This allows the player to produce Titanium Ingots without traveling to the Moon.
Raw Naquadah Ore goes through the usual ore processing and becomes Naquadah Oxide Mixture Dust. Two dust can be processed in the Electric Blast Furnace with 3000L of Fluoroantimonic Acid to produce 4 Titanium Trifluoride Dust, which is then put back into the EBF, which must be overclocked to EV , with 3000L of Hydrogen to get a Hot Titanium Ingot. Cool the ingot in a Vacuum Freezer to obtain a Titanium Ingot.
The production of Fluoroantimonic Acid is an involved process which requires a Large Chemical Reactor that is overclocked to EV. A Distillation Tower is not necessary for the production of Antimony Pentachloride but will refund all of the Ether used in the production of Antimony Trichloride Solution.
The diagram to the right shows the processing steps for obtaining Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. Note that Ethylene and Hydrogen Sulfide are considered inputs, rather than being part of the production chain, as they can be obtained in great quantities from processing Oil and its byproducts.

Chunk.title: Insane Voltage (IV)
section_paths: Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > The Platline
Chunk.text:
The Platline
The Platinum Line , known as the Platline for short, is the central chemical line of IV, and is one of the most complex chemical lines in the entire pack, with approximately 50 steps in total. Although the first part of the platline, which yields Platinum itself, should be done already in EV, the rest, for Palladium, Rhodium, Ruthenium, Iridium, and Osmium, is required to progress into further tiers as well as for many useful upgrades and quality of life improvements within IV. These include the IV Energy Hatch, the Infinite Spray Can (a spray can with access to all 16 colors and infinite uses, for coloring cables), the Vajra (a tool to instantly break any block), and the HSS-S Coils for upgrading the Electric Blast Furnace and other multiblocks. It is possible to run the platline manually as well, in order to obtain small amounts of platline materials to afford key upgrades without needing to build the entire line immediately; for example, an IV Energy Hatch or two to be able to run certain otherwise impossible recipes, such as Nitinol 60 in an ABS to be able to make a HILE .

Chunk.text:
Flexible
Ores in GT: New Horizons have multiple " routes " you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the "best" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):
- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)
- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)
- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)
While for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.
Every ore in the game will have a different "optimal" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.
You also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators.

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line"
Chunk.text:
MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line"
This shows the simplest version of a "central line" ore processing system. It has one route (priority -2) and is currently useless for anything practical. Gold chest = input and copper chest = output. This shows the second most basic EIO ore processing setup - a central line with an attached macerator round robin module.
EnderIO conduits are your first and cheapest option for creating a truly flexible ore processing system. This system is built around a " central conduit line " which all ores go through, and connected " modules " route ores into machines. Because of its modular nature, it is easy to add new routes or expand old ones. This is made possible due to the EIO conduit " priority " system, which allows us to make override routes.
The priority system for the " central line " design goes as follows:
Priority 0: Override routes. For example, specific ores, rare earths, etc.
Priority -1: Type filter routes. These are your "default" paths that are taken if nothing overrides them.
Priority -2: Output routes. This goes to the final output chest.
The simplest version of this is an input chest set to extract always, some conduits inbetween, and an output chest at -2 priority. Then everything you input (ores, random tinker tools by accident, w/e) will go to the output chest. But obviously this isn't very useful.
So you start adding " modules " to your inbetween conduits. These provide routes for ores to go. Let's start with a macerator module.

Chunk.title: Low Voltage (LV)
section_paths: Low Voltage (LV) > Progression
Chunk.text:
Progression
Progression to MV requires the player to obtain 3 essential materials:
• Gallium -
There is no renewable way to obtain Gallium in LV. The best way is to electrolyze Sphalerite dust, giving an 11% chance for Gallium. Gallium is also obtainable as a byproduct of Zinc ore processing, Zinc Gravel can be purchased with Blacksmith coins at regular enough intervals that it shouldn't be a major issue for now. You can also use XP buckets if you're desperate. With an HV macerator you can obtain more byproducts from ore processing, making Gallium much easier to obtain.
• Arsenic -
Cobaltite is the primary way of obtaining Arsenic in LV. When Cobaltite is blasted in an EBF with oxygen it produces roasted cobalt and arsenic dust. Running roasted arsenic dust through the EBF again results in 3 arsenic ingots per 2 cobaltite. This process is oxygen neutral after electrolyzing the carbon dioxide produced.
• Aluminum -
Aluminum has 2 ways to be obtained in LV, one involves compressing Aluminum dust and blasting the "raw Aluminum" into 1 Aluminum ingot. This recipe is slow and not recommended. The other recipe uses 10 Alumina and 5 cryolite to produce 4 Aluminum ingots. While being more involved, this recipe offers much faster and more power efficient Aluminum.

Chunk.title: High Voltage (HV)
section_paths: High Voltage (HV) > Side Objectives > The End and pre-Moon Titanium
Chunk.text:
The End and pre-Moon Titanium
Diagram showing processing steps for making Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. EBF - Electric Blast Furnace; LCR - Large Chemical Reactor; DT - Distillation Tower.
Eyes of Ender can be made in an HV Chemical Reactor and used to find and activate the End Portal. After defeating the Ender Dragon, the player can travel to the Far End Asteroids where they will occasionally find veins of Naquadah Ore. This allows the player to produce Titanium Ingots without traveling to the Moon.
Raw Naquadah Ore goes through the usual ore processing and becomes Naquadah Oxide Mixture Dust. Two dust can be processed in the Electric Blast Furnace with 3000L of Fluoroantimonic Acid to produce 4 Titanium Trifluoride Dust, which is then put back into the EBF, which must be overclocked to EV , with 3000L of Hydrogen to get a Hot Titanium Ingot. Cool the ingot in a Vacuum Freezer to obtain a Titanium Ingot.
The production of Fluoroantimonic Acid is an involved process which requires a Large Chemical Reactor that is overclocked to EV. A Distillation Tower is not necessary for the production of Antimony Pentachloride but will refund all of the Ether used in the production of Antimony Trichloride Solution.
The diagram to the right shows the processing steps for obtaining Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. Note that Ethylene and Hydrogen Sulfide are considered inputs, rather than being part of the production chain, as they can be obtained in great quantities from processing Oil and its byproducts.

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line"
Chunk.text:
MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line"
This shows the simplest version of a "central line" ore processing system. It has one route (priority -2) and is currently useless for anything practical. Gold chest = input and copper chest = output. This shows the second most basic EIO ore processing setup - a central line with an attached macerator round robin module.
EnderIO conduits are your first and cheapest option for creating a truly flexible ore processing system. This system is built around a " central conduit line " which all ores go through, and connected " modules " route ores into machines. Because of its modular nature, it is easy to add new routes or expand old ones. This is made possible due to the EIO conduit " priority " system, which allows us to make override routes.
The priority system for the " central line " design goes as follows:
Priority 0: Override routes. For example, specific ores, rare earths, etc.
Priority -1: Type filter routes. These are your "default" paths that are taken if nothing overrides them.
Priority -2: Output routes. This goes to the final output chest.
The simplest version of this is an input chest set to extract always, some conduits inbetween, and an output chest at -2 priority. Then everything you input (ores, random tinker tools by accident, w/e) will go to the output chest. But obviously this isn't very useful.
So you start adding " modules " to your inbetween conduits. These provide routes for ores to go. Let's start with a macerator module.

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Flexible
Chunk.text:
Flexible
Ores in GT: New Horizons have multiple " routes " you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the "best" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):
- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)
- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)
- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)
While for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.
Every ore in the game will have a different "optimal" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.
You also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators.

answer.answer: The supplied evidence does not establish a complete gallium-focused EnderIO central-line design at MV, and it does not provide any mercury chemical-bath route details to exclude. It supports the central-line priority scheme (Priority 0 override routes, Priority -1 type filter/default routes, Priority -2 output routes), notes that a thermal centrifuge is used especially for gallium, and gives the basic bauxite routes including the Rutile + Gallium byproduct route, but it does not supply the specific gallium routing steps, mercury chemical-bath route information, or byproduct handling needed to design the line under the no-mercury constraint. Chunk.title: Insane Voltage (IV)
section_paths: Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > The Platline
Chunk.text:
The Platline
The Platinum Line , known as the Platline for short, is the central chemical line of IV, and is one of the most complex chemical lines in the entire pack, with approximately 50 steps in total. Although the first part of the platline, which yields Platinum itself, should be done already in EV, the rest, for Palladium, Rhodium, Ruthenium, Iridium, and Osmium, is required to progress into further tiers as well as for many useful upgrades and quality of life improvements within IV. These include the IV Energy Hatch, the Infinite Spray Can (a spray can with access to all 16 colors and infinite uses, for coloring cables), the Vajra (a tool to instantly break any block), and the HSS-S Coils for upgrading the Electric Blast Furnace and other multiblocks. It is possible to run the platline manually as well, in order to obtain small amounts of platline materials to afford key upgrades without needing to build the entire line immediately; for example, an IV Energy Hatch or two to be able to run certain otherwise impossible recipes, such as Nitinol 60 in an ABS to be able to make a HILE .

Chunk.title: Ultimate Voltage (UV)
section_paths: Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Infrastructure Improvements > Component Assembly Line
Chunk.text:
Component Assembly Line
The Component Assembly Line (CoAL) is a new multiblock for assembling components, such as Electric Motors, Robot Arms, and Sensors. It provides a 25% discount on both resources and time, as well as skipping the Assembly Line , two incredible advantages that mean it should be the only source of components whenever it can be used. The main cost of the CoAL is the 43 tiered Component Assembly Line Casings that determine the maximum available tier of components: a full CoAL takes 688 Electric Motors, 430 Electric Pistons, and 344 Robot Arms of its tier. In UV, both the UV and ZPM CoAL tiers are viable. The ZPM CoAL doesn't help with UV components, but it is much cheaper than the UV CoAL, and still useful for LuV and ZPM superconductors in particular, which are used for Fusion Reactor coils and Wetware Mainframes. The UV CoAL adds the ability to make UV components, but is very expensive, particularly on Americium, until late in the tier.

Chunk.title: Low Voltage (LV)
section_paths: Low Voltage (LV) > GT Electric Machines
Chunk.text:
GT Electric Machines
Machine GUI. Auto-output buttons circled in yellow.
LV Electric machines have some new features that were not available with Steam-age machinery. For example, the steam exhaust is replaced with an automatic output. This output's facing can be changed with a wrench similar to how the exhaust was configured on Steam machines. Just like their Steam counterparts, all electric GT machines cannot be input or output from their front face. To enable automatic output, open the GUI of the machine and click on the button at the lower left corner. There are two automatic output toggle buttons; the left one is for liquid and the right one is for items.
Electrolyzer clay dust recipe. The MV power requirement is circled in yellow.
GregTech machinery is divided by tier, which corresponds to a specific voltage - LV (32 V), MV (128 V), HV (512 V) etc. Most recipes are gated to a specific voltage/tier or higher, which is shown with the recipe in NEI (Not Enough Items). If the recipe requires more than one amp it will also be listed here. Pay careful attention to what tier a recipe requires - with LV machinery, MV and higher recipes are inaccessible.
For example, putting Clay Dust through the Electrolyzer to get Aluminium dust requires 120 EU/t (MV). Since the Basic Electrolyzer is only able to do 32EU/t, this recipe is unavailable until the Advanced Electrolyzer (MV).
Recipes close to the voltage limit for LV (32 EU/t) may cause the machine to request multiple amps, especially if there is any cable loss. A single LV generator will often not be capable of supplying enough power if the machine is placed too far away. Most GT machines will accept up to 2 amps. A second generator or Battery Buffer may be needed to keep a a high cost recipe running. If a machine runs out of power, it will stall resetting any progress but not losing the materials. A soft mallet can be used to temporarily disable a machine to give a buffer time to recharge or wait until more power generation is available.
Some machines require multiple amps to run at all, such as the Arc Furnace and Electric Blast Furnace . The Arc Furnace requires 3 amps to function and can accept up to 7 amps. Checking any recipe for the Arc Furnace will show Usage XX/t, voltage 32 EU/t

Chunk.title: High Voltage (HV)
section_paths: High Voltage (HV) > Progression > Mid-HV
Chunk.text:
Mid-HV
With a more powerful energy infrastructure setup and running Cleanroom, you can start working on EV circuits, perfect for creating the HV Circuit Assembler. The HV Circuit Assembler allows you to make IV circuits, which are necessary for the NASA Workbench. From now on, your copper consumption will greatly increase due to the massive demand from plastic circuit boards.
You will also want to look at the new multiblocks such as the Large Chemical Reactor, Distillation Tower, Oil Cracker, and Vacuum Freezer.
The Large Chemical Reactor might not be absolutely mandatory yet, but has some huge benefits: it has perfect overclocks, meaning that speed will quadruple every tier with ZERO additional power cost, it allows you to stop using cells for liquids, and it gates many extremely useful recipes such as a two-step PTFE recipe (for more LCRs) and one-step sulfuric acid from sulfur. The Distillation Tower will be your most expensive multiblock (requiring about ~56 Stainless Steel ingots for every layer), but the added efficiency in both resource production and energy consumption will make it absolutely worth it in the long run.
The Vacuum Freezer is not absolutely necessary until whenever you need Nichrome coils, but is worth crafting sooner than later. It is much cheaper to craft than you might expect (hopefully you have at least 2 and a half stacks of aluminium laying around at this point?) and massively reduces time and energy consumption for whatever Hot Ingots you may have originally been cooling using the Chemical Bath.
The Multi Smelter looks similar to an EBF but requires half the coils. It has insanely good efficiency and parallels while also being pretty cheap at this point, so it is highly recommended to get. You will most likely only need to build one of this.
Lastly, there are some multiblocks not mentioned previously that are possible to craft now that you have a cleanroom up and running:
- Oil Cracking Unit : Replaces the hydrogen and steam cracking recipes that were done in the Chemical Reactor in previous tiers. It provides power cost reduction and bonus outputs. This is absolutely worth it for anyone using Oil to produce chemicals such as Ethylene.
- Large Sifter : The first unlockable ore processor. It provides a massive boost to speed in the form of raw time reduction as well as parallels. In addition, sifting is a mandatory step in

Chunk.title: Medium Voltage (MV)
section_paths: Medium Voltage (MV) > Goals > Optional Side Quests
Chunk.text:
Optional Side Quests
- Aluminium & defeating the first Twilight Forest boss Naga, which gives the player access to Thaumcraft .
- Create the Good Miner for additional mining range and fortune bonus. Remember that it can be powered by LV generators.
- Use EnderIO Item Conduits to instantly move things around complex networks. The EnderIO conduits have additional bonuses, such as routing, support for item filtering, and the ability to pull from non-output machine sides, but have less throughput without upgrades.
- Use the Tool Forge to fill out your set of Tinker's Construct Hammer/Excavator/Scythe/Cleaver and other tools.
- Convert single-block steam/LV machines to their MV counterparts, or upgrade to Steam multiblocks ( Steam Oven , Steam Grinder , Steam Squasher , etc).
- Start Bees or IC2 Crops for renewable resources.
- Botania & Witchery.

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Expandable
Chunk.text:
Expandable
Depending on what batch you are processing, you may find a major bottleneck in your current system, or you simply want to replace machines with multis. This means your system must be able to expand without causing catastrophic infrastructure redesigns. Ideally you only want to change stuff in the current step you're dealing with (eg thermal centrifuging), not the whole line.

Chunk.text:
The Rest of the Line
Every module you add will look almost exactly like the macerator module. The only things you will swap out will be different filters and machines in place of the macerators.
For specific item overrides (eg. I want crushed bauxite specifically to go to thermal centrifuging), remember to use priority 0, as this will override items going to the normal macerator route we defined above.
On the right you can see an example of a fully fledged EIO ore processing line.

Side quest 2: Multiblock ore processing
As you entered EV, you gained access to multiblock counterparts of centrifuge, thermal centrifuge, ore washer/chemical bath, and crusher. Chunk.text:
Flexible
Ores in GT: New Horizons have multiple " routes " you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the "best" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):
- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)
- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)
- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)
While for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.
Every ore in the game will have a different "optimal" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.
You also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators.

Chunk.title: High Voltage (HV)
section_paths: High Voltage (HV) > Progression > End Of HV
Chunk.text:
End Of HV
After collection of ores from the Moon, check NEI on how to make Titanium (you process everything into Rutile then react it with Carbon Dust and Chlorine). You will need a stack for turning in the titanium quest to enter the EV tier in the questbook. Note that you must cool Titanium using a Vacuum Freezer after smelting in the EBF.
Spending some time now looking for a Moon dungeon is an excellent idea too. The mobs are not tough if you've been keeping up at all with your armor, weapons, and health bar. In addition, you are guaranteed to find a T2 rocket schematic in the loot chest (which you absolutely need to progress out of early EV in a standard run), and the quest book will grant you access to your own personal dimension!
Infrastructure for processing Rutile into Titanium, and Bauxite specifically is recommended, as they are relatively simple multi-step processes and their reactants (not all of Bauxite's, though) can be recycled very simply. Remember, you will be consuming dozens of stacks of Titanium in EV!

Chunk.title: Zero Point Module (ZPM)
section_paths: Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Infrastructure Improvements > Neutronium
Chunk.text:
Neutronium
Neutronium is a new material that is needed in very large quantities in UV and UHV for components and other machines, and it is extremely slow to smelt, taking over two minutes at UV even with the best possible noble gas, and closer to three or four with worse ones. Because of how slow it is and how much it is used, most players passive it, setting up either a Mega Electric Blast Furnace (MEBF) or a large Volcanus array dedicated to passively smelting Neutronium Ingots. The MEBF can be scaled more easily and is much simpler to set up, but due to the high voltage and heat requirements for the Neutronium recipe and the 120% speed bonus of the Volcanus, the latter is more efficient. It is also possible to smelt Neutronium entirely on demand, but doing so requires extremely robust smelting and freezing capacity, or it will be a massive bottleneck.

Chunk.title: Zero Point Module (ZPM)
section_paths: Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Progression > Fusion Reactor Mk2 > Americium
Chunk.text:
Americium
Americium is incredibly slow in the Mk2 Fusion Reactor, taking 43.2 seconds per ingot and 34 minutes for enough ingots for a single UV Electric Motor. It is much slower than Europium: it takes three times as long to produce, and twice as much is used in each motor. Methods for dealing with this include making it passively, either in multiple reactors or over many days on a server, or even making a Compact Fusion Reactor for players whose infrastructure, resources, and power can support it. In UV, many better methods of making Americium will become available, including the Americium Bee in a Mega Apiary , a Meteor containing thousands of Americium Dust worth of ore, and a much faster recipe in the Mk3 Fusion Reactor; however, all of them require large amounts of Americium to reach.

Chunk.title: Insane Voltage (IV)
section_paths: Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines
Chunk.text:
Other chemical lines
Polybenzimidazole
Although the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.
Rare Earths
The rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank .

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Flexible
Chunk.text:
Flexible
Ores in GT: New Horizons have multiple " routes " you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the "best" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):
- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)
- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)
- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)
While for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.
Every ore in the game will have a different "optimal" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.
You also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators.

Chunk.title: High Voltage (HV)
section_paths: High Voltage (HV) > Progression > End Of HV
Chunk.text:
End Of HV
After collection of ores from the Moon, check NEI on how to make Titanium (you process everything into Rutile then react it with Carbon Dust and Chlorine). You will need a stack for turning in the titanium quest to enter the EV tier in the questbook. Note that you must cool Titanium using a Vacuum Freezer after smelting in the EBF.
Spending some time now looking for a Moon dungeon is an excellent idea too. The mobs are not tough if you've been keeping up at all with your armor, weapons, and health bar. In addition, you are guaranteed to find a T2 rocket schematic in the loot chest (which you absolutely need to progress out of early EV in a standard run), and the quest book will grant you access to your own personal dimension!
Infrastructure for processing Rutile into Titanium, and Bauxite specifically is recommended, as they are relatively simple multi-step processes and their reactants (not all of Bauxite's, though) can be recycled very simply. Remember, you will be consuming dozens of stacks of Titanium in EV!

section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2
Chunk.text:
Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.
For our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:
- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices, giving our 1-block controller control over a maximum of 192 devices.
- ME Drive. This will serve as an overflow buffer, just in case all your machines suffer maintenance issues and shutdown simultaneously.
- ME Storage Cell. Place inside the ME Drive. You will need at least 1.
- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.
- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).
- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.
Now, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:
- Galena Ore. oreGalena
- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena
- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena
- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena
- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena
- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena
- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena
- Galena Dust dustGalena
ME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Thus, when we place an OreDict card inside a ME Storage Bus facing towards an Input Bus, we have created an intelligent exporter of items!

section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2
Chunk.text:
EV Applied Energistics 2
Applied Energistics (henceforth just referred to as AE) is the most commonly used logistics system for mid-late game. As such, it finds common use in high-tier ore-processing solutions designed by players. From EV - ZPM, the multiblock miners ( Ore Drilling Plants I/II/III/IV)(ODPs) become available. At IV and beyond (up to a point), single-block machines are no longer acceptable for the amount of ores we will be processing, and instead we will move on to the GT++ multiblock machines. These are:
- Ore Washing Plant (OWP)
- Maceration Stack (MS)
- Large Thermal Refinery (LTR). This is the multiblock thermal centrifuge.
- Industrial Centrifuge (IC)
- Large Sifter (LS).
- Industrial Electrolyzer (IE)
- Utupu-Tanuri / Dehydrator (only necessary for Rare Earths and a few Toxic Everglades ores)
Other multiblock machines that we will be using are the Large Chemical Reactors (LCRs).
For a typical ore processing setup at EV - ZPM, we generally have the following desires.
- Maximise returns. If we throw in an ore that has tertiary byproducts, we want all the byproducts. This requires use of a thermal centrifuge. Thus, our system will make use of thermal centrifuges, especially for gallium
- Maximise throughput. ODPs are capable of immense output, and an inadequate setup will choke and die. In addition, Void Miners (VMs) become available near the tail end of this period, and these will overwhelm unprepared systems, especially when boosted with the noble gases.
- Indium retrieval. Indium is a particular metal needed for specific circuit components (namely as indium gallium phosphide, or InGaP). There are various ways to get this metal. Replication with UU-Matter (slow and painful), fusion from lithium and silver (requires T3 Fusion , unlocked in UV ), milling sphalerite (unlocked in LuV ), processing Naquadria (unlocked in LuV ), processing Roquesite or pure Indium ore (extremely rare) or extraction from purified Sphalerite and Galena ores .
- Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.

Chunk.title: Zero Point Module (ZPM)
section_paths: Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Infrastructure Improvements > Neutronium
Chunk.text:
Neutronium
Neutronium is a new material that is needed in very large quantities in UV and UHV for components and other machines, and it is extremely slow to smelt, taking over two minutes at UV even with the best possible noble gas, and closer to three or four with worse ones. Because of how slow it is and how much it is used, most players passive it, setting up either a Mega Electric Blast Furnace (MEBF) or a large Volcanus array dedicated to passively smelting Neutronium Ingots. The MEBF can be scaled more easily and is much simpler to set up, but due to the high voltage and heat requirements for the Neutronium recipe and the 120% speed bonus of the Volcanus, the latter is more efficient. It is also possible to smelt Neutronium entirely on demand, but doing so requires extremely robust smelting and freezing capacity, or it will be a massive bottleneck.

Chunk.title: Zero Point Module (ZPM)
section_paths: Zero Point Module (ZPM) > Infrastructure Improvements > Noble Gases
Chunk.text:
Noble Gases
Both smelting (including Neutronium smelting) and Void Miners can be vastly improved by using a high-tier noble gas. Oganesson is not practically obtainable in ZPM, but the next steps down, Xenon and Krypton, are. There are two methods of obtaining these gases: their respective bees or the Planetary Gas Siphon (PGS). The PGS is best used for Xenon, which requires a Tier 6 Rocket; each PGS can collect 350 L/s of Xenon when fed with 2A of ZPM. Bees are much more efficient on power, but the Xenon Bee cannot be used yet because it requires the Mega Apiary , meaning Krypton is the best noble gas available from bees in ZPM.

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Flexible
Chunk.text:
Flexible
Ores in GT: New Horizons have multiple " routes " you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the "best" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):
- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)
- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)
- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)
While for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.
Every ore in the game will have a different "optimal" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.
You also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators.

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line"
Chunk.text:
MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line"
This shows the simplest version of a "central line" ore processing system. It has one route (priority -2) and is currently useless for anything practical. Gold chest = input and copper chest = output. This shows the second most basic EIO ore processing setup - a central line with an attached macerator round robin module.
EnderIO conduits are your first and cheapest option for creating a truly flexible ore processing system. This system is built around a " central conduit line " which all ores go through, and connected " modules " route ores into machines. Because of its modular nature, it is easy to add new routes or expand old ones. This is made possible due to the EIO conduit " priority " system, which allows us to make override routes.
The priority system for the " central line " design goes as follows:
Priority 0: Override routes. For example, specific ores, rare earths, etc.
Priority -1: Type filter routes. These are your "default" paths that are taken if nothing overrides them.
Priority -2: Output routes. This goes to the final output chest.
The simplest version of this is an input chest set to extract always, some conduits inbetween, and an output chest at -2 priority. Then everything you input (ores, random tinker tools by accident, w/e) will go to the output chest. But obviously this isn't very useful.
So you start adding " modules " to your inbetween conduits. These provide routes for ores to go. Let's start with a macerator module.

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > LV GregTech Item Pipes + Type Filters
Chunk.text:
LV GregTech Item Pipes + Type Filters
Automated ore processing is possible as early as LV because of the introduction of GregTech's Item Pipes and Filter blocks. The item pipes are extremely limited compared to future tiers' logistics solutions, but they have some key properties that make them usable for automation, while having major caveats:
- The flow of items within a network of pipes can be in any direction.
- Items put into a pipe network are pushed into the "closest" inventory that accepts them.
- Distance is measured by routing value, where higher routing value means higher distance.
- The distances of inventories can be coarsely manipulated using restricted item pipes which have extremely high routing values.
Combining this with GregTech's Item Filter, Recipe Filter, and/or Type Filter blocks, which are capable of selectively accepting and automatically outputting items, enables a functional framework for ore processing. This system should ideally be hooked up to the steam multiblocks for maceration , washing , and centrifuging , as the LV singleblock counterparts have much worse throughput.
One way this system can be implemented with a centralized pipe network that connects to all machine input and outputs, as well as an input and output chest. Each machine input needs a Recipe Filter or Type Filter block in front of it, so that the only inputs going into each machine are inputs that the machine can handle. Another way to do it is to have multiple Type Filters that output into a separate pipe subnetwork that then outputs into a machine. For example, a Steam Grinder can be hooked up to a Recipe Filter block set to Macerator so that it accepts any item that can be macerated, or it could be hooked up to Type Filter blocks for specific stages, such as Raw, Crushed, Impure, or Purified.

section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2
Chunk.text:
EV Applied Energistics 2
Applied Energistics (henceforth just referred to as AE) is the most commonly used logistics system for mid-late game. As such, it finds common use in high-tier ore-processing solutions designed by players. From EV - ZPM, the multiblock miners ( Ore Drilling Plants I/II/III/IV)(ODPs) become available. At IV and beyond (up to a point), single-block machines are no longer acceptable for the amount of ores we will be processing, and instead we will move on to the GT++ multiblock machines. These are:
- Ore Washing Plant (OWP)
- Maceration Stack (MS)
- Large Thermal Refinery (LTR). This is the multiblock thermal centrifuge.
- Industrial Centrifuge (IC)
- Large Sifter (LS).
- Industrial Electrolyzer (IE)
- Utupu-Tanuri / Dehydrator (only necessary for Rare Earths and a few Toxic Everglades ores)
Other multiblock machines that we will be using are the Large Chemical Reactors (LCRs).
For a typical ore processing setup at EV - ZPM, we generally have the following desires.
- Maximise returns. If we throw in an ore that has tertiary byproducts, we want all the byproducts. This requires use of a thermal centrifuge. Thus, our system will make use of thermal centrifuges, especially for gallium
- Maximise throughput. ODPs are capable of immense output, and an inadequate setup will choke and die. In addition, Void Miners (VMs) become available near the tail end of this period, and these will overwhelm unprepared systems, especially when boosted with the noble gases.
- Indium retrieval. Indium is a particular metal needed for specific circuit components (namely as indium gallium phosphide, or InGaP). There are various ways to get this metal. Replication with UU-Matter (slow and painful), fusion from lithium and silver (requires T3 Fusion , unlocked in UV ), milling sphalerite (unlocked in LuV ), processing Naquadria (unlocked in LuV ), processing Roquesite or pure Indium ore (extremely rare) or extraction from purified Sphalerite and Galena ores .
- Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.
For our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:
- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices,

End Of HV
After collection of ores from the Moon, check NEI on how to make Titanium (you process everything into Rutile then react it with Carbon Dust and Chlorine). Spending some time now looking for a Moon dungeon is an excellent idea too. The mobs are not tough if you've been keeping up at all with your armor, weapons, and health bar. In addition, you are guaranteed to find a T2 rocket schematic in the loot chest (which you absolutely need to progress out of early EV in a standard run), and the quest book will grant you access to your own personal dimension!
Infrastructure for processing Rutile into Titanium, and Bauxite specifically is recommended, as they are relatively simple multi-step processes and their reactants (not all of Bauxite's, though) can be recycled very simply. Remember, you will be consuming dozens of stacks of Titanium in EV!

section_paths: Extreme Voltage (EV) > Progression > Side quest 2: Multiblock ore processing
Chunk.text:
Side quest 2: Multiblock ore processing
As you entered EV, you gained access to multiblock counterparts of centrifuge, thermal centrifuge, ore washer/chemical bath, and crusher. They are way more efficient compared to their singleblock variants, however they require large amounts of resources like Titanium and most are gated behind TPV coils, so they're listed here instead of in early EV. If your main resource income is from bees, centrifuge is recommended over all other multiblocks as it speeds up centrifuging combs significantly.

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > EV Applied Energistics 2
Chunk.text:
Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.
For our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:
- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices, giving our 1-block controller control over a maximum of 192 devices.
- ME Drive. This will serve as an overflow buffer, just in case all your machines suffer maintenance issues and shutdown simultaneously.
- ME Storage Cell. Place inside the ME Drive. You will need at least 1.
- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.
- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).
- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.
Now, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:
- Galena Ore. oreGalena
- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena
- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena
- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena
- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena
- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena
- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena
- Galena Dust dustGalena
ME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Thus, when we place an OreDict card inside a ME Storage Bus facing towards an Input Bus, we have created an intelligent exporter of items!
