Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line"
Chunk.text:
MV EnderIO Conduits - The "Central Line"
This shows the simplest version of a "central line" ore processing system. It has one route (priority -2) and is currently useless for anything practical. Gold chest = input and copper chest = output. This shows the second most basic EIO ore processing setup - a central line with an attached macerator round robin module.
EnderIO conduits are your first and cheapest option for creating a truly flexible ore processing system. This system is built around a " central conduit line " which all ores go through, and connected " modules " route ores into machines. Because of its modular nature, it is easy to add new routes or expand old ones. This is made possible due to the EIO conduit " priority " system, which allows us to make override routes.
The priority system for the " central line " design goes as follows:
Priority 0: Override routes. For example, specific ores, rare earths, etc.
Priority -1: Type filter routes. These are your "default" paths that are taken if nothing overrides them.
Priority -2: Output routes. This goes to the final output chest.
The simplest version of this is an input chest set to extract always, some conduits inbetween, and an output chest at -2 priority. Then everything you input (ores, random tinker tools by accident, w/e) will go to the output chest. But obviously this isn't very useful.
So you start adding " modules " to your inbetween conduits. These provide routes for ores to go. Let's start with a macerator module.

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Flexible
Chunk.text:
Flexible
Ores in GT: New Horizons have multiple " routes " you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the "best" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):
- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)
- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)
- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)
While for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.
Every ore in the game will have a different "optimal" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.
You also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators.

Chunk.title: Insane Voltage (IV)
section_paths: Insane Voltage (IV) > Progression Goals > Other chemical lines
Chunk.text:
Other chemical lines
Polybenzimidazole
Although the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.
Rare Earths
The rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank .

How To Do "Good" Ore Processing?
Bauxite ore processing page accessible in NEI, showcasing various processing routes and their outputs
Although there are many implementations of doing ore processing, the desired features of a "good" solution remain the same. These desirable characteristics are:
- Flexible
- Expandable
- Unbreakable
- High Throughput
- Lag Friendly
- Minimal Human Intervention

Chunk.title: Extremely Ultimate Voltage (UEV)
section_paths: Extremely Ultimate Voltage (UEV) > Progression > Waterline
Chunk.text:
Waterline
Like LuV , ZPM , and UV , UEV brings two new steps to the Waterline , one of which is required in the tier and one of which is not required until the next tier but increases yield of components for optical circuits. The Residual Decontaminant Degasser Purification Unit and its associated Grade 7 water are needed to process Optically Enriched Crystalline Boules to make UIV circuits. After making the DTPF , the Absolute Baryonic Perfection Purification Unit and its Grade 8 water and Stabilised Baryonic Matter can increase the yield of raw optical enhanced chips by 2.25x per boule over Grade 7, and are required for Dimensionally Shifted Superfluid, which is used in many recipes beginning at UIV.
The Degasser, used for grade 7 water

Chunk.title: Ultimate Voltage (UV)
section_paths: Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Progression > Waterline
Chunk.text:
Waterline
Like ZPM, UV brings two new steps to the Waterline, one of which is required in the tier and one of which is not required except as an ingredient to the next grade of water. The Extreme Temperature Fluctuation Purification Unit and its associated Grade 5 water are needed to process Americium-Doped Wafers, which are needed for QPIC Wafers for the Mk3 Fusion Reactor. The High Energy Laser Purification Unit and Grade 6 water are not required until UEV when Grade 7 water must be made, but since it is a significant improvement over Grade 5, and UHV will require large amounts of wafers, it's generally advisable to make it sooner than that. Grade 6 or above water is also required for the most advanced Beam Line masks.

This shows the simplest version of a "central line" ore processing system. It has one route (priority -2) and is currently useless for anything practical. Gold chest = input and copper chest = output. This shows the second most basic EIO ore processing setup - a central line with an attached macerator round robin module.
EnderIO conduits are your first and cheapest option for creating a truly flexible ore processing system. This system is built around a " central conduit line " which all ores go through, and connected " modules " route ores into machines. Because of its modular nature, it is easy to add new routes or expand old ones. This is made possible due to the EIO conduit " priority " system, which allows us to make override routes.
The priority system for the " central line " design goes as follows:
Priority 0: Override routes. For example, specific ores, rare earths, etc.
Priority -1: Type filter routes. These are your "default" paths that are taken if nothing overrides them.
Priority -2: Output routes. This goes to the final output chest.
The simplest version of this is an input chest set to extract always, some conduits inbetween, and an output chest at -2 priority. Then everything you input (ores, random tinker tools by accident, w/e) will go to the output chest. But obviously this isn't very useful.
So you start adding " modules " to your inbetween conduits. These provide routes for ores to go. Let's start with a macerator module.

EV Applied Energistics 2
Applied Energistics (henceforth just referred to as AE) is the most commonly used logistics system for mid-late game. As such, it finds common use in high-tier ore-processing solutions designed by players. From EV - ZPM, the multiblock miners ( Ore Drilling Plants I/II/III/IV)(ODPs) become available. At IV and beyond (up to a point), single-block machines are no longer acceptable for the amount of ores we will be processing, and instead we will move on to the GT++ multiblock machines. These are:
- Ore Washing Plant (OWP)
- Maceration Stack (MS)
- Large Thermal Refinery (LTR). This is the multiblock thermal centrifuge.
- Industrial Centrifuge (IC)
- Large Sifter (LS).
- Industrial Electrolyzer (IE)
- Utupu-Tanuri / Dehydrator (only necessary for Rare Earths and a few Toxic Everglades ores)
Other multiblock machines that we will be using are the Large Chemical Reactors (LCRs).

Chunk.title: Ore Processing Concepts
section_paths: Ore Processing Concepts > How To Do "Good" Ore Processing? > Flexible
Chunk.text:
Flexible
Ores in GT: New Horizons have multiple " routes " you can take which give different outputs. (See the bauxite chart to the right.) For bauxite you can take three routes (Note that these choices simply outline the basic bauxite processing and are not meant to show the "best" way to process bauxite, realistically you will probably want to do chembath and/or bauxite slurry):
- Macerate -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Grossular byproduct)
- Macerate -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerate (Rutile + Gallium byproduct)
- Macerate -> Simple/Normal Wash -> Macerate -> Simple Wash/Centrifuge (Rutile + Grossular (if normal wash) byproduct)
While for most bases, Rutile + Gallium Route 2 is superior, perhaps you already have automated gallium from essence berries. Then you might decide to do Route 3 instead, as it gives 2x more Rutile and therefore 2x more Titanium.
Every ore in the game will have a different "optimal" route for your run and base needs. This may also change over time. As a result, you want ore processing systems to be flexible - allowing different ores to go on different routes.
You also want to be able to automatically pull out things at any step of the process. For example, Rare Earths from GT++ require much higher power load, which would cause your existing macerator line to choke without modifications. You'll want to filter these out and process them in specially dedicated macerators.

Chunk.text:
Lanthanide processing. This processing line takes in crushed Bastnasite or crushed Monazite to yield the different lanthanide elements.
For our purposes, we will only need 6 specific AE components in order to create a rudimentary, and yet infinitely expandable AE ore processing system:
- ME Controller. This is basic and fundamental. You will need at least 1 to be the brains of your ore processing subnet. Each exposed face can connect to and control up to 32 other AE devices, giving our 1-block controller control over a maximum of 192 devices.
- ME Drive. This will serve as an overflow buffer, just in case all your machines suffer maintenance issues and shutdown simultaneously.
- ME Storage Cell. Place inside the ME Drive. You will need at least 1.
- ME Interfaces (the full block type). These will serve as the import blocks, from which the outputs of your machines will be pushed into to enter the AE network. How many you need depends on how creative you are with your GT piping.
- ME Storage Buses. You will need 1 for each input bus of your multiblock machines, and one extra to handle overflow (optional).
- ME OreDictionary Filter Cards. This is the magic that makes AE amazing for ore processing. You will need at least 1 per storage bus, with some exceptions.
Now, let's talk more about the ME OreDictionary Filter Card, or OreDict cards for short. Many GT items have an OreDictionary Name, that looks something like (item type)(name) . There are OreDict names for the ore block, each of the intermediates during the ore processing steps, and the final pure dust. Using galena as an example, they are:
- Galena Ore. oreGalena
- Raw Galena Ore. rawOreGalena
- Crushed Galena Ore. crushedGalena
- Purified Galena Ore. crushedPurifiedGalena
- Centrifuged Galena Ore. crushedCentrifugedGalena
- Impure Pile of Galena Dust dustImpureGalena
- Purified Pile of Galena Dust dustPureGalena
- Galena Dust dustGalena
ME Storage Buses attempt to push out compatible items, when immediately received by the network via either ME Interfaces or ME Import Buses, into the inventories that they face. Conventionally, these would be storage blocks like chests/drawers/barrels. But note that Input Buses also have internal inventories. Thus, when we place an OreDict card inside a ME Storage Bus facing towards an Input Bus, we have created an intelligent exporter of items!

section_paths: Extreme Voltage (EV) > Progression > Side quest 2: Multiblock ore processing
Chunk.text:
Side quest 2: Multiblock ore processing
As you entered EV, you gained access to multiblock counterparts of centrifuge, thermal centrifuge, ore washer/chemical bath, and crusher. They are way more efficient compared to their singleblock variants, however they require large amounts of resources like Titanium and most are gated behind TPV coils, so they're listed here instead of in early EV. If your main resource income is from bees, centrifuge is recommended over all other multiblocks as it speeds up centrifuging combs significantly.

Chunk.title: High Voltage (HV)
section_paths: High Voltage (HV) > Side Objectives > The End and pre-Moon Titanium
Chunk.text:
The End and pre-Moon Titanium
Diagram showing processing steps for making Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. EBF - Electric Blast Furnace; LCR - Large Chemical Reactor; DT - Distillation Tower.
Eyes of Ender can be made in an HV Chemical Reactor and used to find and activate the End Portal. After defeating the Ender Dragon, the player can travel to the Far End Asteroids where they will occasionally find veins of Naquadah Ore. This allows the player to produce Titanium Ingots without traveling to the Moon.
Raw Naquadah Ore goes through the usual ore processing and becomes Naquadah Oxide Mixture Dust. Two dust can be processed in the Electric Blast Furnace with 3000L of Fluoroantimonic Acid to produce 4 Titanium Trifluoride Dust, which is then put back into the EBF, which must be overclocked to EV , with 3000L of Hydrogen to get a Hot Titanium Ingot. Cool the ingot in a Vacuum Freezer to obtain a Titanium Ingot.
The production of Fluoroantimonic Acid is an involved process which requires a Large Chemical Reactor that is overclocked to EV. A Distillation Tower is not necessary for the production of Antimony Pentachloride but will refund all of the Ether used in the production of Antimony Trichloride Solution.
The diagram to the right shows the processing steps for obtaining Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. Note that Ethylene and Hydrogen Sulfide are considered inputs, rather than being part of the production chain, as they can be obtained in great quantities from processing Oil and its byproducts.

Chunk.title: Ultimate Voltage (UV)
section_paths: Ultimate Voltage (UV) > Progression > Cosmic Neutronium > Meteors
Chunk.text:
Meteors
Another option for players with enough magic progress is meteors , specifically the UV Crop Synthesizer meteor, which is unlocked with UHV circuits. If boosted with Orbis Terrae, this meteor contains around 2000 Cosmic Neutronium Ore when mined with Arcane Bores or manually, and triple that if an Ore Drilling Plant is used instead. By summoning them repeatedly, it's possible to amass very large quantities before getting access to the ore through the Space Elevator. The meteor also has other very useful ores, including a similar amount of Americium Ore, as well as Infinity Catalyst Ore, which can be used for earlier access to Infinity.
